url.description: An http or https URL with a host and no credentials: a password in a URL is a secret in the file, and a secret is named, never carried.

description: The policy document: what an installation decides, read by every process of it. The access model's tables (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md) and beside them whom the exchange trusts, what an operator may make, what each controller may change and what is copied out. Rendered by `sluisctl policy render` from layers; a process reads exactly one. Nothing here is a secret.

apiVersion.description: Which version of which document this is. sluis.truvity.github.io/policy/v2 is what this build writes; a document with no apiVersion is v1, which the binary converts as it loads it, and a binary reads v2 and v1 (docs/reference/sluis/configuration.md).

apps.description: What an operator may make on the console.

Every GitHub App the installation declares, of every purpose: the link App, the catalogue Apps and the runner tiers (docs/guides/sluis/connect/github-apps-catalogue.md). A grant naming an undeclared group stops the service.

items.description: One App. A `catalogue` entry needs `org` and `permissions`; a `runner` entry needs `tier` and declares nothing of a catalogue App's; the `link` entry has the id `link`.

events.description: Webhook events the App subscribes to. They are delivered only to an App that declares a `webhook`.

export.description: Place the installed App's key at `external/github/<id>` for a consumer to read. Unset keeps it internal. A runner App is always exported.

grants.description: Who may ask for tokens of it, and for how much.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

id.description: The App's key in storage, unique, never changes. `link` for the link App; for a catalogue App [a-z0-9-], at most 32, not beginning `runner-`; a runner entry may leave it out (`runner-<tier>`, and `runner-<tier>-<org>` with an `org`).

labels.description: At most 16 short lower-case labels, key to value, kept on the App's record for a reader that selects Apps by them.

org.description: The organisation a catalogue App is created under (required for it), or the only organisation of a runner entry (no `org` offers the tier in every organisation). The link App's owner.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

purpose.description: What the App is for: `link` is the App that links a person's GitHub account, `catalogue` an App an operator creates and installs from the console, `runner` the tier an operator may create a runner App for.

tier.description: A runner entry's tier: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 16.

webhook.description: Where GitHub delivers the App's events: exactly one of `url` and `kargo`. Needs non-empty `events`; set `export: true` so a consumer can read the secret. The secret is generated by this service, set on GitHub right after the App is created, and kept at `external/github/<id>` as `webhook_secret`; it is rotated from the console, without overlap (docs/decisions/0041). An App created before this is declared cannot be switched to a webhook: GitHub has no API for that, so disconnect it and create it again.

kargo.description: A Kargo GitHub receiver. Kargo derives the receiver's path from its secret (`/github/<hex sha256(project + receiver + secret)>`), so the URL moves whenever the secret does.

project.description: The Kargo project; empty for a cluster-scoped receiver.

receiver.description: The receiver's name in the Kargo project.

url.description: The endpoint every delivery is POSTed to, e.g. Argo CD's `https://argocd.example/api/webhook`.

catalogue.description: DEPRECATED, removed in v1.77: declare each as a `purpose: catalogue` entry in `apps`. Read as those entries, with a warning.

items.description: One App: created under `org` from the console, and installed there.

events.description: Webhook events the App subscribes to. They are delivered only to an App that declares a `webhook`.

export.description: Place the installed App's key at `external/github/<id>` for a consumer to read. Unset keeps it internal. An id may not begin `runner-`.

grants.description: Who may ask for tokens of it, and for how much.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

org.description: The organisation it is created under.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

webhook.description: Where GitHub delivers the App's events: exactly one of `url` and `kargo`. Needs non-empty `events`; set `export: true` so a consumer can read the secret. The secret is generated by this service, set on GitHub right after the App is created, and kept at `external/github/<id>` as `webhook_secret`; it is rotated from the console, without overlap (docs/decisions/0041). An App created before this is declared cannot be switched to a webhook: GitHub has no API for that, so disconnect it and create it again.

kargo.description: A Kargo GitHub receiver. Kargo derives the receiver's path from its secret (`/github/<hex sha256(project + receiver + secret)>`), so the URL moves whenever the secret does.

project.description: The Kargo project; empty for a cluster-scoped receiver.

receiver.description: The receiver's name in the Kargo project.

url.description: The endpoint every delivery is POSTed to, e.g. Argo CD's `https://argocd.example/api/webhook`.

runnerTiers.description: DEPRECATED, removed in v1.77: declare a `purpose: runner` entry in `apps` for each tier. Read as those entries, with a warning.

catalogue.description: Every Slack App the installation declares (docs/guides/sluis/connect/slack-apps-catalogue.md). One for a workspace the policy does not declare stops the service.

items.description: One Slack App, created and installed from the console.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

additionalProperties.description: A claims fragment: merged into the token (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#claims).

claims.description: What a group adds to a token, by group.

client_documents.description: Admits clients that are not declared, by a document they serve about themselves. Off unless it names an origin.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold.

session.description: Every document client's refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Never read from a document: admit with `agent` only an origin whose documents its vendor controls.

additionalProperties.description: A client: who may be issued a token, and for what. Its id is the audience.

backchannel_logout_uri.description: Where a back-channel logout is posted.

description.description: One line about it on the sign-in page. Public.

display_name.description: What the sign-in page calls it. Public.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold, any of them.

secret.description: For a confidential client: the name its secret is delivered under, or `{generate: true}` to have the issuer generate it and keep it with its credentials.

generate.description: Must be true; `generate: false` is refused.

session.description: Its refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Refused on an exchange client and, as `agent`, with `sign_in_exchange`.

sign_in_exchange.description: It may exchange a sign-in for a token of its own.

signed_out.description: Where sign-out may return the browser.

signing_alg.description: The algorithm its tokens are signed with, when it cannot verify the default: RS256, ES256 or ES384.

ttl_cap.description: The longest a token for it lives.

clients.description: Who may be issued a token, by client id.

cloudflare.description: Who may ask for a Cloudflare preset (the presets are the service document's `cloudflare.presets`). A preset named here and not there stops the service.

group.description: A group of this policy: every holder may ask, a person from the console or `sluisctl`, a CI job through the exchange. A CI job is a group declared with `github` matchers.

controllers.description: What each controller may CHANGE. Everything else the policy binds is derived every pass and shown with what would happen, and left alone: an organisation or workspace is born disabled.

appRefs.description: For an organisation the github table binds, the id of the catalogue App (in `apps.github.apps`, created under that organisation) whose key its record refers to, `app_ref`. Optional: an organisation whose record already names an App keeps it, so an entry only overrides it or declares an organisation anew.

enabledOrgs.description: The organisations it changes. Each must be bound by the github table.

enabledWorkspaces.description: The workspaces it changes, by key. Each must be declared by the slack table.

exchange.description: Whom the token exchange trusts. Nothing here is a secret: every row is a name and a URL.

aws.description: The AWS accounts whose roles' outbound identity tokens (sts:GetWebIdentityToken) are verified. An empty list verifies none.

name.description: The estate's word for it, for logs.

audience.description: The audience the role must request. Required with an account: it is the trust boundary.

maxAge.description: Refuse a token whose `iat` is older than this. At most 1h.

clusters.description: The clusters whose ServiceAccount tokens are verified, each against the key set it publishes for itself. This service's own cluster is a row like any other.

jwksUri.description: Where its keys are. Unset discovers them from the issuer.

name.description: The estate's word for it: the cluster in a `service_account` matcher. Renaming a row changes every rule about it.

github.description: Whose GitHub Actions tokens are verified, for this issuer's URL as the audience.

owners.description: The organisations. None verifies none: an empty list would admit every repository there is.

ignore.description: Addresses and logins the controller leaves alone.

members.description: The groups whose holders belong in the organisation.

maintainers.description: The groups whose holders are maintainers.

members.description: The groups whose holders are members.

github.description: GitHub organisations bound to internal groups, by login.

items.description: One way a caller comes to be in the group. Exactly one kind is set.

aws.description: An IAM role in an account `exchange.aws` federates.

email_domain.description: Every signed-in address in a domain.

github.description: A GitHub Actions job, by what its verified token says.

job_workflow_ref.description: The reusable workflow at a ref, a glob.

workflow_ref.description: The workflow file at a ref, a glob.

service_account.description: A ServiceAccount on a federated cluster.

cluster.description: The cluster's name in `exchange.clusters`. Unset is the unqualified subject.

members.description: Directory groups whose members are in it.

groups.description: Every internal group, by name, and how a caller comes to be in it.

lifetimes.description: How long a token lives, by group, and `default`. The shortest across a caller's groups wins.

people.description: Which addresses are one person, by a name the installation chooses.

additionalProperties.description: A resource a token may be minted for, when it is not the client asking.

absolute_cap.description: The longest a session that touched it lives.

display_name.description: What the consent page calls it.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

read_only.description: It only reads: an absolute cap past the installation's may be honoured. Deprecated as a lengthening (docs/decisions/0040): mark the clients `session: agent` instead; a lengthening row is warned about at start.

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold, any of them.

signing_alg.description: The algorithm its tokens are signed with: RS256, ES256 or ES384.

ttl_cap.description: The longest a token for it lives.

resources.description: What a token may be minted FOR, by resource indicator.

slack.description: Slack channels bound to internal groups, across workspaces.

from.description: The groups whose holders belong in it.

workspaces.description: Each workspace, by the installation's key.

vocabulary.description: Which scopes, things and roles a grant name may use, and each thing's role ladder. Optional: absent, any `<scope>:<thing>:<role>` is accepted unchecked.

additionalProperties.description: A role: the roles it implies, or `{implies, scopes}` to restrict it to some of its thing's scopes.

scopes.description: The scopes it may be exercised on.
